utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case scheduled on today's roll.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, this is case number IT-95-9-A, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, can you hear and follow the procedure in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask the parties for the appearances, please. I'm turning to the Office of the Prosecutor first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Steffen Wirth appearing for the Prosecution, together with Peter Kremer, and our case manager is Ms. Lourdes Galicia and Ms. Kim Fischer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. May I have the appearances of the Defence counsel of Mr. Simic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, my name is Peter Murphy and I also represent the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic has filed a notice to the appeal against a judgement rendered on the 17th of October, 2003. Whilst awaiting the Appeals Judgement Mr. Simic is detained at the UN Detention Unit at The Hague in the Netherlands. Pursuant to the provisions of Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Status Conference is convened within 120 days of the filing of the notice and every 120 days to allow the person in custody, pending appeal, the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto including the mental and physical condition of the person. Mr. Simic, do you have any concerns or do you have any issues to raise in relation to your mental and physical condition or in relation to the condition, detention conditions?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no matters to raise today. I have no particular comments in relation to either the conditions in the detention or my health condition for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. On 3 February 2006 the Appeals Chamber has decided proprio motu -- granted proprio motu the access to confidential material relating to medical charts of Mr. Stevan Todorovic filed before the Trial Chamber in the Todorovic case. These medical records relate to the 16th ground of appeal of Mr. Simic. We acknowledge receiving the Prosecution's notice on 8 February 2006, and we are awaiting the time -- the delays to expire while awaiting the allow -- while awaiting Mr. Todorovic to request protective measures relating to the redaction of certain parts of the report. I would like to remind the Defence of Mr. Simic that the order granting this provision is so that they will have seven days to file any additional submissions, and there is going to be a precise schedule for eventually rebuttals and rejoinders. I would like to draw the attention of the parties that only imperative reasons will allow the schedule to change. And finally, regarding the oral submissions, the circumstances have not allowed the Appeals Chamber to find a correct -- or a date for the end of this month. The appeals hearing was postponed for Monday, 20 March, 2006, at 9.00. I would like to ask Mr. Registrar to kindly hand and send the parties a schedule -- Scheduling Order, to kindly hand the parties the Scheduling Order regarding today's appeal hearing. Would you kindly hand those orders. Thank you. Thank you very much. And lastly, the Appeals Chamber has received a joint motion filed by the parties on 19 January 2006 in which the Prosecution and the Defence request to be kept abreast of issues and particular points that the Chamber wishes to raise during the appeals hearing, at least four weeks prior to the hearing. If the Scheduling Order does not draw to the attention of the party issues of that type, the Appeals Chamber will inform the parties as soon as the circumstances will allow it. I have no further issues to raise. I am inviting the parties to make any observations or to raise issues that they would like to be addressed. I'm turning to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing further to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have one matter to raise which refers to the Court's order proprio motu regarding the medical records of Mr. Todorovic. Your Honour, my understanding is that a Mr. Kostic, who may be representing Mr. Todorovic as counsel, has written a letter in which he does seek some protective measures with regard to the records. And my understanding from the Office of the Prosecutor is that he has been given until the 20th of this month, that would be next Monday, to submit -- to make those submissions, after which I think we would then have some time to respond pursuant to the Court's order. Your Honour, my concern is this: If the medical records are released to the Defence, Mr. Pantelic and I would of course wish to have the benefit of some expert advice to -- to tell us, really, whether there is anything material in those records to help the Court with the ground of appeal, the 16th ground of appeal. And while we would try to do that as quickly as possible, I'm not sure exactly how long it would take. We would have to, of course, ask the permission of the registry to retain an expert witness, and if the expert were to advise us that there was something material in the records, we might then, at that stage, file a motion allowing -- asking to be allowed to file the expert report with the Court as additional evidence. Your Honour, I mention that simply because the Court has given us a schedule for the continued conduct of the appeal, and while we expect to be ready without any difficulty to meet that, and we are prepared to argue the case at any time, Your Honour, there is that outstanding matter of evidence which we will try to move along as fast as possible, but there is some possibility that it may take a little longer than we think. And I just want to draw the Court's attention to that in case we should have to make a motion at some stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Do you have anything to add on that particular point?

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not at the time. We would -- we would respond to any motion from the Defence when the time comes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. We will take into account what the parties have said. We will try to find a solution to your problems, as you have presented it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are there any other issues, further issues to raise? No, I see. Very good. This being said, this hearing stands adjourned. I thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: adjourned at 8.12 a.m.
